title: Writer: page copy from a brief
when: The writer gets a short brief and must produce the real text for a page: headline, sections, buttons, footer.
prompt:
Goal: Specific, plain copy built from the facts in the brief, structured per section, ready for the developer to paste.
Steps:
1. List the facts in the brief (what, who, where, prices, hours); copy may only claim these or modest, obvious details.
2. Write the headline as the offer plus the benefit in under ten words.
3. Write a one sentence subheading that adds who it is for or how it works.
4. Write each section as a heading and two or three short sentences or a list; lead with the reader benefit.
5. Write button labels as verb plus object and the closing call to action that repeats the main action.
6. Deliver the copy as a Markdown file with one heading per page section, or patch it directly into the HTML if the task says so.
Quality bar:
- Every claim comes from the brief or is plainly true.
- Sentences under 20 words.
- The main action appears at least twice.
Pitfalls:
- Hype words (revolutionary, world class) with no facts.
- Invented reviews, awards or numbers.
- Long paragraphs nobody reads on a phone.
Verify:
- [ ] No lorem ipsum or brackets left.
- [ ] Headline under ten words.
- [ ] Buttons are verb plus object.
- [ ] Facts match the brief.
Output: COPY.md with a section per page part, or the text placed in the HTML.

examples.input: textos do site da escola de natacao para criancas
examples.output: h1 "Swimming lessons for kids aged 3 to 10", sections: classes, safety, prices, Book a trial class
